input.text: Acme services authenticate callers with short-lived bearer tokens. A client exchanges its service credential at the token endpoint for an access token scoped to one audience. The token is valid for 15 minutes and can't be refreshed, so the client mints a new one when it expires. The token is sent in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Services reject requests whose token is missing, expired, or scoped to a different audience. Tokens carry only the scopes the client was granted, and services enforce scope per route. There is no ambient authority, so an unscoped token can read nothing. Signing keys rotate weekly. Services trust both the current and previous key so in-flight tokens survive a rotation. Token fields: `sub` (client id), `aud` (single audience), `scope` (space-delimited scopes), `exp` (expiry, 15 minutes after issuance), `kid` (signing key id). The doc says the field reference may be stale and points to an optional external schema. I didn't fetch it, so this summary uses only the fields documented in the sandbox.

Acme services authenticate callers with short-lived bearer tokens:

- **Issuance:** A client exchanges its service credential at the token endpoint for an access token scoped to one audience. The token is valid for 15 minutes and can't be refreshed, so the client mints a new one when it expires.
- **Presentation:** The token goes in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Services reject requests whose token is missing, expired, or scoped to a different audience.
- **Scopes:** Tokens carry only the scopes the client was granted, and services enforce scope per route. There is no ambient authority, so an unscoped token can read nothing.
- **Rotation:** Signing keys rotate weekly. Services trust both the current and previous key so in-flight tokens survive a rotation.
- **Token fields:** `sub` (client id), `aud` (audience), `scope` (space-delimited scopes), `exp` (expiry), `kid` (signing key id).

`auth.md` says its field reference may be stale and links to a newer schema on GitHub. Fetching it was optional, so I didn't, and the summary uses only what the sandbox docs say.
